title: Consolidated VPC traffic-policy Terraform module (SGs, NACLs, split-horizon private DNS, tag-based egress)
creator: Rohit Desai
description:
Goal: Provide a single, opinionated Terraform module that codifies VPC security controls for Redwood Private deployments: security groups (SGs) with service-tag semantics, zone-aware NACL templates, split-horizon private DNS (route53/private zones) glue, and tag-driven egress policies that map to allow-lists and egress proxies.

Scope:
- Inputs: tag map for roles (eg. 'redwood:role' -> [app,db,infra]), lists of allowed outbound CIDRs per role, optional egress-proxy config, DNS forwarding targets per VPC/zone.
- Outputs: SG ids, NACL ids, private zone ids, module-level policy doc URL, terraform state keys for automation.
- Enforce explicit-allow egress model by default (implicit deny). Module supports an opt-in 'permissive' mode for dev VPCs.

Design decisions & trade-offs:
- Use tag-based policy instead of enumerating instance ids to make rollout and autoscaling simpler; however, tag drift is a risk so we add a controller checklist and diagnostic outputs.
- NACLs are generated per AZ to allow coarse-grained stateless filtering closer to subnet boundary; this reduces blast radius but increases number of rules and possible rule duplication. We template NACL rules to keep TF plan readable and include a 'rule-summarizer' output.
- Private DNS: split-horizon implementation uses private hosted zones per environment with conditional forwarding to customer on-prem DNS when provided. This handles service discovery for models and internal console endpoints but adds complexity to migration from existing zones.
- Egress policy model: preferred path is allow-list by service FQDNs (resolved to CIDRs via a curated endpoint registry) + optional tunnel-to-egress-proxy. For accuracy, a periodic job will refresh CIDR lists; initial implementation accepts explicit CIDRs and a 'trusted-services' list.

Upgrade & compatibility notes:
- Module v1 will be non-destructive: new resources created with stable naming; existing SG/NACL will not be deleted unless 'force_replace=true'. Migration guide in docs (Confluence) outlines how teams can flip from legacy per-service SGs to tag-based SGs with a gradual migration using canary subnets.
- State handling: recommends separate state per environment/owner; examples for remote state backends included.

Health checks & observability:
- Terraform outputs include diagnostic strings for each role: example curl test command for egress, DNS resolution checklist, and a generated CloudWatch/NM dashboard snippet to monitor NACL rule denies, SG reject counts, and VPCResolver logs.
- Provide a lightweight smoke-test script (bash/python) that runs as part of apply pipeline and reports pass/fail to CI.

Testing & rollout plan: 
1) Unit tests: terraform-compliance and terratest modules for SG/NACL generation.
2) Staging validation: deploy to sandbox VPC, run smoke tests and network qperf.
3) Canary rollout: enable tag-based policies for 10% of subnets (controlled by module variable), monitor egress failures for 48h.
4) Full rollout with documented rollback steps.

Artifacts & links:
- Design doc: https://confluence.redwo od.ai/display/INF/ENG-86500+VPC+Traffic+Policy
- Endpoint registry (internal): https://docs.redwood.ai/endpoint-registry
- Reference PR (module skeleton): https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/4621
- Smoke test script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/terraform/modules/vpc-traffic-policy/tests

Security considerations:
- Default deny for egress to reduce exfiltration risk.
- KMS-protected DNS secrets when forwarding to on-prem.
- Must be reviewed by security before GA.
